svg.text: Sheet 2 — Sensing node front end (one board, used for both nodes; gain and divider by jumpers) + Nucleo-H743ZI2
4th-order Butterworth low-pass, f_c = 100 kHz (two Sallen-Key sections; values are the design starting point,
finalised with the measured step response). Feature band-pass tops out at 100 kHz; converter ripple ≥ 400 kHz is ≥ 48 dB down.
JP1 replay: lifts the U1 output and feeds the SMA input (from the bench-control DAC) into the same filter and ADC
R6/R7: rack 12 V: 20 k / 4.7 k (÷5.3); feeder 48 V: 100 k / 4.99 k (÷21); 0.1 % metal film; jumper selects
same 4th-order 100 kHz filter as the current channel
USB FS (event records to the PC)
PF13 TRIP — to breaker gate driver (Sheet 3) + LED
PB8 / PB9 CAN-FD — U7 TCAN1042, 120 Ω termination
PE9 role jumper — open = rack, closed = feeder
Power: 3.3 V from the Nucleo; analog rail through a ferrite bead with 10 µF + 100 nF at every amplifier.
Full scale: rack 13 × rated at 2.6 V (1 mΩ × 130 A × 20); feeder 2 × rated. Rated current = ~4 000 LSB of 16 bits.
Pins: firmware/node/board.h (PA3, PC0, PF13/14/15, PF12, PE9, PD8/PD9 VCP). Change board.h if the header pins differ.
INA240 gain options: A1 = 20, A2 = 50, A3 = 100, A4 = 200 V/V. The first design note wrote A3 for ×50; it is A2.
Deliberately NOT on the bench node: galvanic isolation (common ground), the external 14-bit SAR ADC (the H7 internal 16-bit ADC is used). Both are product items.
